stage: the address to building to parcel to door bindings, and what the registry really covers

result.registry: the settlement registry declares twenty-seven addresses, each with a buildingId, a parcelId, an addressId, a street and number, a role and optionally a primaryDoor
result.doors: two addresses declare a primaryDoor, and both node names (HeroHouse_StreetDoorClosed_LOD0 and MosqueEntranceDoor) really exist in the authored scene, so a relocation would carry the door it binds
result.aliases: the three aliases (ADR-SHOP to ADR-H020, ADR-SCHOOL to ADR-H031, ADR-COUNCIL to ADR-H040) all point at declared addresses, so a quest naming the shop address resolves
result.coverage: five of the registry's (street, number) pairs land on records of kind kit in the authored scene, and the seventy-nine bulk parcels of the grid are not covered by it. That is NOT a defect and is reported as the registry's own declared scope, quoted from its source line: these bindings do not move geometry
result.own_mistakes: three of my first versions were wrong and are recorded: I compared the registry with workspace entities (parcel ids are not indexed at all, they lack the namespace:kind/name shape), I read only kind=parcel records (which made the coverage look like zero) although the registry binds kind=kit records, and I initially called thirty referenced addresses unresolved before checking the alias table

verified.probe: PASS 540/540 with the new checks: twenty-seven addresses read, a declared door present, every door found in the scene, every alias resolvable, and the uncovered count reported as the registry's scope rather than as a defect
verified.compile: Urman.Studio.Core 0 warnings/0 errors; game/Urman.Game.csproj 0 warnings/0 errors
verified.not_run: no game run: whether a moved house, its interior and its doors end up in the right place is a runtime and visual question, NOT_RUN

open: the moving itself still needs the runtime: this stage proves the bindings resolve, not that a relocation is consistent on screen
